taxonomy_mapping_dispositions.reason: A face-swapped applicant used false AI-mediated identity in a paid-job application and interview, materially supporting an attempted economic inducement.
The synthetic applicant advanced to interview but was detected before any consequential hiring decision, materially marking the boundary between questionable identity evidence and decision authority.
A synthetic face was used in the hiring attempt, but the record does not identify an attributable real person whose likeness or authority state can be established.
The face-swapped applicant presented a false identity in a remote hiring interview, obtaining a consequential screening opportunity even though Pindrop flagged the deception before hiring.
Pindrop’s detection assistant flagged the face swap during screening; the record shows a further interview but neither the intended blocking threshold nor a final hiring decision.

retained_rows.assessment_basis: Pindrop reports that the applicant presented a synthetic visual identity as an ordinary person during a paid-role interview; the employer discovered the face swap through its own detector, with no reported applicant disclosure of the AI-mediated representation. The initial presentation therefore failed the workplace-interaction awareness benchmark in this bounded first-party account. Later detection supplied awareness but did not make the earlier deceptive presentation transparent. The result does not assert a hire, liability or generator-wide controls.

The employment interview's AI face-swap detector makes MEASURE 1.2 materially relevant. Regular assessment/update of detection metrics and control effectiveness is not preserved; one flagged example cannot establish its cadence or reliability. This independent outcome concerns the detector/control workflow rather than formal adoption or generator-side conformance.

The employment interview's AI face-swap detector makes MEASURE 2.5 materially relevant. The detection validation/reliability demonstration and documented generalisation limits are unavailable; successful flagging of this example is not full validation. This independent outcome concerns the detector/control workflow rather than formal adoption or generator-side conformance.
retained_rows.identification_basis: The preserved AI detector flagging a synthetic interview identity directly identifies reliability/validation and generalisation limits independently of the held FC derivation.

retained_rows.assessment_basis: The actual synthetic-face detector directly engages the contemporaneous NIST technical detector proposition. The detector's representative-data, transformation and adversarial evaluation and uncertainty results are unavailable; flagging one case is not proof of that full evaluation. The result concerns evidentiary completeness, independently of adoption and of the attempted solicitation taxonomy finding.
